newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH TPSA LOSES BILLION ZLOTYS IN FLOOD - PM.
newsitem.headline: POLISH TPSA LOSES BILLION ZLOTYS IN FLOOD - PM.

text.p: State-owned telecoms company Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) has lost one billion zlotys during the floods in southern Poland, Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told parliament on Wednesday.
"Telekomunikacja Polska suffered enormous losses which are estimated to amount to over one billion zlotys," Cimoszewicz told an emergency session of the parliament.
Communications Minister Andrzej Zielinski said the high costs of repairing the flood damage may harm plans to develop the country's telecommunications.
"The degree of devastation of the telephone network, especially the cable network, may affect the development programmme of telecommunications in Poland," he said.
"The estimated losses total around 30 percent of investment expenditure," Zielinski told parliament.
TPSA plans to go public after the government agreed in May to float up to 25 percent of the telecoms monopolist in 1998 on Polish and international markets.

TPSA's revenues increased to 6.7 billion zlotys last year from 5.4 billion in 1995, while net profit fell to 850 million zlotys ($270 million) last year from 933 million in 1995 due to extensive investment. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
